transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

What finally made me come in is that I’m having a hard time staying with things at work. I’ll start an EPIC quality report or sit in a clinic metrics meeting really intending to follow along, and within a few minutes my mind has drifted. Then I’m rereading the same numbers over and over, or I realize I missed the main point of what was just discussed. It’s becoming hard to ignore.
Did you have similar trouble paying attention when you were a child?

Yes. Looking back, I think it was there even in elementary school. Teachers would say I was bright, but careless. My mom had to sit with me to get homework done because I’d lose track of assignments or forget my books at school.
Do you also have this same kind of trouble staying focused in other parts of your life, outside of work?

Yes, it’s not just work. The same kind of thing happens when I’m trying to focus on anything that takes sustained attention. I’ll sit down fully intending to follow along or get through something, and after a few minutes I realize my mind has wandered and I have to reread or catch myself up. It’s frustrating because I’m trying, but I just don’t stay with it.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety?
Not really, no. I mean, I might shift around like anyone else, but I don’t think of myself as especially restless or fidgety.
Do you often feel anxious or worried?
Not especially. I mean, I worry about normal things, like work or family stuff, but I wouldn’t say I’m anxious all the time or that worry is the main issue for me.
I’m not sure. I don’t think sleep is a major problem for me, but I’d have to think about it. I haven’t really noticed a consistent issue there.
Do these attention problems also interfere with managing things at home?

Yes, it does, though I notice it more with responsibilities outside the house than with chores. At work, when I get delayed, it affects clinic reporting deadlines and other teams end up waiting on me. And I’ve had to step back from leading parts of the volunteer health workshops because I just couldn’t reliably keep the planning pieces moving.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get frustrated with myself sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed feeling down or depressed lately.
